confirmed.title: mu shift is applied twice: the pipeline re-shifts the sigmas the backend already shifted
confirmed.description: `_shifted_sigmas()` applies `sigma' = e^mu / (e^mu + (1/sigma - 1))` and passes the result as `sigmas`. `Krea2Pipeline` does not treat `sigmas` as a final schedule: it computes its own mu and forwards it to the scheduler alongside them (pipeline_krea2.py:613-631), and `FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler.set_timesteps` shifts unconditionally when dynamic shifting is on (scheduling_flow_match_euler_discrete.py:348-349 -> `_time_shift_exponential`, which is byte-for-byte the backend's formula). Verified in this environment: the cached `krea/Krea-2-Turbo` scheduler_config.json has `"use_dynamic_shifting": true` and its model_index.json has `"is_distilled": true`, so the pipeline's own mu is the hard-coded 1.15. The exponential shift composes additively (it multiplies the odds s/(1-s) by e^mu), so the effective shift is mu_user + 1.15. CLAUDE.md's rationale ("`Krea2Pipeline.__call__` accepts `sigmas`, not `mu`") is true of the signature but misses that the pipeline injects its own mu behind `sigmas`. FluxPipeline has the identical structure (pipeline_flux.py:821-840), so an API client taking the schema default `mu=1.15` double-shifts there too.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Generate on krea/Krea-2-Turbo with the profile defaults (steps=8, mu=1.15). The intended schedule [1.0, 0.957, 0.905, 0.840, 0.760, 0.655, 0.513, 0.311] is replaced by the shift(2.30) schedule [1.0, 0.986, 0.968, 0.943, 0.909, 0.857, 0.769, 0.588]: nearly all 8 steps are spent at high noise and the final Euler step drops sigma from 0.588 to 0 in one jump, giving soft, under-resolved output. Every Turbo image the app has produced is affected, and Reuse reproduces the same wrong schedule, so nothing looks inconsistent.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Compensate for the shift the pipeline will apply, or stop pre-shifting. Since the shift composes additively, pass `self._shifted_sigmas(request.steps, request.mu - pipeline_mu)` where `pipeline_mu` is 1.15 when `getattr(pipe.config, "is_distilled", False)` and `calculate_shift(image_seq_len, ...)` otherwise - at the default mu=1.15 that collapses to the raw `1 - i/steps` grid, exactly what the pipeline uses on its own. Guard on `getattr(pipe.scheduler.config, "use_dynamic_shifting", False)`, and test the schedule the *scheduler* ends up with, not the one the backend computes.

confirmed.title: 63-bit seeds lose precision in JS, so Reuse silently reproduces a different image
confirmed.description: `jobs._generate` draws `random.randint(0, 2**63 - 1)` whenever `req.seed is None` - the default, since the seed box ships empty and the dice button clears it. `ImageRecord.seed` (schemas.py:54) is serialized as a bare JSON number, and 99.9% of that range is above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, so `res.json()` rounds it. Everything downstream uses the rounded value: `reuse()` writes it into the seed box (app.js:397), `renderLightbox()` prints it (app.js:419), `collect()` posts it back (app.js:193). Measured: 7283207964119141687 parses as 7283207964119141000. `storage.save_image` puts the *true* seed in the filename and the PNG metadata, so the file is right and only the UI is wrong - which makes the failure invisible. This defeats commit 2922c44 ("Make Reuse actually reproduce the image") and CLAUDE.md's guarantee that an image is reproducible from its recorded seed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Leave the seed box empty and generate. The server records seed 7283207964119141687 and names the file for it; the lightbox reports 7283207964119141000. Click Reuse, then Generate: the pipeline seeds a generator with the rounded value and produces a visibly different image while the UI claims the settings were reproduced. Seeds within ~512 of the maximum round *up* past `le=2**63-1` and make Generate fail with a 422 rendered as a stringified pydantic error list.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Cheapest correct fix: stop minting seeds JS cannot hold - change the random draw's `_MAX_SEED` to `2**53 - 1` in backend/jobs.py:26 and backend/generate.py:40, leaving the column and the request bound at 2**63-1 for hand-entered seeds. Alternative: serialize `ImageRecord.seed` as a string (`field_serializer`), accept `int | str` on `GenerateRequest.seed`, and treat it as opaque in reuse()/renderLightbox()/collect(). Either way add a regression check that a 19-digit recorded seed survives Reuse exactly.

confirmed.title: Unload during a running job frees no VRAM and makes the worker silently reload the pipeline mid-sweep
confirmed.description: `unload_model()` (main.py:114-118) and the shutdown hook (main.py:72) call `backend.unload()` with no coordination against `jobs._gate` or `_load_lock`. `DiffusersBackend.unload()` takes only `self._lock`, which `generate()` never holds, so `self._pipe` becomes None under a job that is still denoising - and because the worker holds a local `pipe` reference (diffusers_backend.py:216) with the transformer resident, no VRAM is actually freed while `/api/status` reports "unloaded". The next run of the sweep then hits `if self._pipe is None: self.load()` (diffusers_backend.py:212-213) and re-materialises ~13 GB on the generation worker thread while holding the gate - exactly the second load path CLAUDE.md says must not exist ("Loading happens in exactly one place: main.ensure_loaded()"). Worse, `_run` awaits `ensure_loaded()` *outside* `_gate` (jobs.py:142-152), so a job submitted after the unload starts a second concurrent `from_pretrained` while the first is still generating. There is also a narrow window between the None check (212) and the re-read (216) where `pipe` is None and the run dies with `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not callable`. The UI invites all of it: `setBusy()` (app.js:199-207) disables only Generate and Cancel, leaving the Unload button live.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Submit a 64-run 2048x2048 sweep. Midway, click Unload. The endpoint returns 200 and the status dot flips to "not loaded", but nvidia-smi shows VRAM unchanged for the rest of the current run. The worker then begins the next run, finds `self._pipe is None`, and reloads the whole quantized pipeline on the "gen" thread - minutes of frozen progress bar with the status still reading "not loaded" - then continues for another half hour. Any job queued in that window runs a second `from_pretrained` in parallel, holding two copies of the weights. The same sequence fires on server Ctrl-C: lifespan unloads, the worker reloads and keeps generating, and the non-daemon pool thread keeps the terminal from returning after "Application shutdown complete".
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make unload mutually exclusive with generation: add a `busy()` helper to JobManager (`self._gate.locked()`) and have `POST /api/model/unload` answer 409 while a job is non-terminal, or serialize it under `_load_lock`. In `lifespan`, set `cancel_requested` on every non-terminal job and `jobs._pool.shutdown(wait=True)` before unloading. Replace the `if self._pipe is None: self.load()` fallback in `generate()` with a raise so the single-load invariant is enforced rather than papered over, and disable the Unload button in `setBusy()`.

confirmed.title: No Host-header validation: DNS rebinding gives any website full read and delete on the API
confirmed.description: The app is created with no `TrustedHostMiddleware` (no middleware of any kind exists in backend/). Binding to 127.0.0.1 stops off-machine TCP connections but not a browser on the user's own machine being pointed at loopback by a hostile DNS record. Because the server accepts any `Host`, a rebound name becomes a legitimate origin for it and CORS stops applying - the attacker page reads responses directly. Every endpoint is unauthenticated: `GET /api/gallery?limit=200` (all prompts and metadata), `GET /outputs/<filename>` (every PNG), `DELETE /api/images/{id}`, `POST /api/generate`. An Origin check alone does not fix it, since same-origin GETs carry no Origin header.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Victim runs the server on the default 127.0.0.1:7860 and visits attacker-controlled `http://evil.example:7860`, served with a TTL-1 A record that is re-answered as 127.0.0.1 after the page loads. The page's `fetch('/api/gallery?limit=200')` is same-origin from the browser's point of view, reaches the local server, and every prompt the user has ever typed plus every filename is readable by attacker JS. A follow-up loop of `fetch('/api/images/'+id, {method:'DELETE'})` over the returned ids deletes the rows and unlinks the PNGs.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add a Host allowlist at app construction: `app.add_middleware(TrustedHostMiddleware, allowed_hosts=["127.0.0.1", "localhost"])` (it strips the port before comparing). If `settings.host` is set to something non-loopback, extend the list from it rather than dropping the middleware.

confirmed.title: Body-less POST endpoints are CSRF-able: any page can unload the model or clear every favorite
confirmed.description: `POST /api/model/unload` (114), `/api/model/load` (107), `/api/jobs/{id}/cancel` (145) and `/api/images/{id}/favorite` (187) declare no body parameters - `favorite` takes `value: bool = True` as a *query* parameter the attacker controls in the URL. A cross-origin `fetch(url, {method:'POST', mode:'no-cors'})` is a CORS simple request: no preflight, the browser only refuses to let the page read the response, and the server executes it. There is no CSRF token, no Origin check, and no cookie/SameSite barrier because the app has no auth at all. `POST /api/generate` is not reachable this way (FastAPI only json-parses application/json, so a simple content type 422s) and DELETE is preflighted, but these four are open.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The user is 40 minutes into a 64-run sweep and opens any tab that loads attacker or ad-network JS doing `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:7860/api/model/unload',{method:'POST',mode:'no-cors'})` - the sweep then silently reloads ~13 GB mid-run (see the unload finding). Or the same page runs `for (let i=1;i<10000;i++) fetch('http://127.0.0.1:7860/api/images/'+i+'/favorite?value=false',{method:'POST',mode:'no-cors'})`; ids are a sequential AUTOINCREMENT key, so this walks the whole table and clears every starred image.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Reject state-changing methods that arrive with a foreign Origin - a small `@app.middleware("http")` that 403s when `request.method not in (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS)` and `request.headers.get("origin")` is present and not in `{http://127.0.0.1:{port}, http://localhost:{port}}`. Browsers attach Origin to every POST, so curl and the CLI keep working.

confirmed.title: Negative prompt silently dropped for 0 < CFG <= 1 while Krea2 still runs the uncond pass
confirmed.description: The guard is `if request.negative_prompt and request.guidance_scale > 1.0:`. That threshold is the SD/FLUX true-CFG convention and is right for FluxPipeline, but wrong for Krea2Pipeline, which turns guidance on above 0.0 - verified in this venv at pipeline_krea2.py:426-427 (`return self._guidance_scale > 0`) and :666 (`noise_pred + guidance_scale * (noise_pred - neg_noise_pred)`). In the band 0 < guidance_scale <= 1.0 the backend strips the user's negative prompt, and the pipeline then substitutes an empty one (pipeline_krea2.py:582-584) and runs the second transformer forward every step anyway. CLAUDE.md's stated justification ("CFG is inactive at or below 1.0, so the negative prompt is dropped there rather than wasting an encoder pass") is incorrect for the pipeline this app is built around: that band is precisely where the cost is paid and the input discarded.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On krea/Krea-2-Turbo submit prompt="a portrait", negative_prompt="blurry, watermark", guidance_scale=0.5. The backend omits `negative_prompt`; the pipeline sees `do_classifier_free_guidance == True`, encodes "" as the negative, and runs two transformer passes per step. The user pays double the generation time and is guided away from the empty prompt instead of away from "blurry, watermark", with no warning - while the stored ImageRecord still records the negative prompt, so Reuse looks faithful.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Gate on the parameter the pipeline actually exposes rather than assuming one convention: if `"true_cfg_scale" in self._call_params` keep the `> 1.0` rule (FLUX), else pass the negative prompt whenever `guidance_scale > 0.0` (Krea2). Turbo's default of 0.0 still takes the single-pass path with no negative encode, which is the real saving the current code was after. Correct the CLAUDE.md bullet at the same time.

confirmed.title: GenerateRequest hardcodes Krea-2-Turbo's profile while settings.model_id defaults to FLUX
confirmed.description: `steps=8` (15), `guidance_scale=0.0` (16) and `mu=1.15` (18) are the `krea-2-turbo` row of `model_defaults._PROFILES`, copied into the request schema. Commit d826124 changed `settings.model_id` to `black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev`, whose profile is 28 steps / CFG 3.5 / mu None, and the schema was never reconciled. CLAUDE.md names `model_defaults.py` as the source of truth and states that forcing Turbo's mu on FLUX degrades output, yet the schema hands FLUX mu=1.15 for every request that omits the field. The browser normally papers over it via `applyDefaults`, but only after a successful `/api/status` - and `refreshStatus` swallows every error while `status()` can answer minutes late. index.html:44-46 is a third copy of the same three numbers.
confirmed.failure_scenario: `curl -X POST localhost:7860/api/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"prompt":"a lighthouse in fog"}'` on a stock install runs FLUX.1-Krea-dev at 8 steps, CFG 0.0, and an explicit mu=1.15 sigma schedule that overrides FLUX's own resolution-dependent shift - an undersampled, degraded image with no warning. The same happens in the browser if the user hits Generate or Ctrl+Enter before the first `/api/status` lands, since index.html's static control values are the same Turbo constants.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Default `steps`/`guidance_scale`/`mu` to None and fill them from `defaults_for(settings.model_id)` in a `@model_validator(mode="after")` (or via `default_factory`), so the profile table is the only place these numbers live. `model_defaults` imports nothing, so there is no cycle. Update index.html's static `value=` attributes to match.

confirmed.title: LIKE fallback in list_images silently drops the favorites filter and miscounts total
confirmed.description: `list_images` builds one `where`/`params` pair that correctly ANDs `favorite = 1` with the FTS predicate (170-177), but the `except sqlite3.OperationalError` branch (186-196) hand-writes a second, independent COUNT/SELECT pair against `WHERE prompt LIKE ?` with the favorites clause gone from both. The fallback is not exotic: line 176 wraps each token in double quotes without escaping embedded ones, so any search containing an odd number of `"` produces a malformed MATCH. Reproduced here against the real schema: search `26"` becomes `"26""` -> `OperationalError: unterminated string`, and the LIKE fallback then returned both the favorited and the non-favorited row under `favorites_only=True`. The fallback also interpolates the term into LIKE without escaping `%`/`_`, so a search for `50%` wildcards mid-term.
confirmed.failure_scenario: With the Favorites checkbox ticked, the user searches `26"` (a lens, a monitor) or `a 6" figure`. The FTS COUNT raises, the except swallows it, and the gallery fills with non-favourite images while the count badge reports every matching row. Paging walks a result set the user never asked for, so "Load more" pulls in still more non-favourites, and nothing tells the user the search degraded.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Delete the second query pair. In the except branch replace only the search predicate in the existing list (`where[-1] = "prompt LIKE ? ESCAPE '\\'"; params[-1] = like`), rebuild `clause`, and run the same COUNT/SELECT through a shared local helper so the two paths can never disagree on filters, ORDER BY or paging again. Escape `%`, `_` and `\` in the LIKE term.

confirmed.title: clear_history's orphan sweep deletes PNGs of an in-flight generation and aborts on a locked or vanished file
confirmed.description: `save_image` writes the PNG at line 140 and only inserts its row at 142-163, so a valid image exists on disk with no row for a window of hundreds of milliseconds. `clear_history` snapshots `keep` at line 263 and unlinks every `*.png` not in it (265-268). `_write_lock` gives no protection: it is a per-process `threading.Lock` and `backend/clear.py` runs in a separate process, while clear.py's docstring and the README advertise exactly this concurrent use ("Safe to run while the server is up"). Line 267 also unlinks with no `missing_ok` and no `except OSError` - unlike delete_image (218) and the doomed loop (258-259) - and `summarise()` has the same shape at line 234 with an unguarded `stat()` over a second glob.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A 64-run sweep is in progress and the user runs `uv run python -m backend.clear --yes` as the docs say is safe. (a) The worker finishes `image.save()` for run 40; `_tracked_files()` snapshots `keep` before its INSERT commits; the sweep unlinks the file - the gallery now lists a record whose `/outputs/<name>.png` 404s permanently, and no future orphan sweep will clean it up because the row *is* tracked. (b) If the sweep reaches a PNG while PIL still holds the handle, `path.unlink()` raises `PermissionError [WinError 32]` out of clear_history *after* the row DELETE is committed, so vacuum never runs and the remaining orphans are left untracked on disk.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Only treat a file as an orphan once it has settled - skip anything whose `st_mtime` is within the last ~60 s - or write to a `.png.part` name the glob cannot match and rename after the INSERT commits. Use `path.unlink(missing_ok=True)` at 267 (and drop the redundant `exists()` at 258-259 in favour of it), wrap each unlink in `try/except OSError: continue`, and make `summarise()`'s size sum tolerant of a file that disappears between glob and stat.

confirmed.title: A reload or one dropped SSE frame orphans a running sweep: no way to see or cancel it
confirmed.description: The job id lives only in the JS variable `currentJob` (app.js:46/223). Nothing persists it (no localStorage/sessionStorage anywhere in app.js) and the server exposes no way to enumerate jobs — main.py has only `/api/jobs/{job_id}`, `/cancel` and `/stream`, all keyed by an id the client must already hold. Two routine events destroy that id while the job keeps running: (1) a page reload, and (2) `source.onerror` at app.js:288, which calls `source.close()` and `setBusy(false)` — and `setBusy(false)` nulls `currentJob` at line 206. The `close()` is the sharper half: EventSource would otherwise reconnect on its own, and the server is explicitly built to support that (jobs.py:234-247 replays a status/done snapshot and the undrained `job.queue` still holds every event emitted while the client was away). Closing the source cancels the browser's retry, so one blip is permanent. Nothing on the server notices either: the disconnect cancels only the StreamingResponse task, never `_run`, so the sweep continues to hold `self._gate` (jobs.py:152) and the GPU.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Start a 64-run 4 MP sweep (hours). Press F5, or the tab is discarded / the connection blips once. The reloaded page shows state 'ready', an idle Generate button and no hint that a job is running. The user clicks Generate: the new job's `_run` blocks on `self._gate` behind the orphan, so its stream only ever delivers a `status` snapshot with status 'queued', which app.js:269 ignores (it handles only `status === 'running'`). The progress text sits at 'queued…' (app.js:215) for hours with no run/step/queue-position feedback. Cancel (app.js:238) cancels the new job, not the blocker. The orphaned sweep cannot be reached at all — the only way to stop it is killing the server.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Persist `job_id` (sessionStorage) on submit and reattach on page load; add `GET /api/jobs` returning non-terminal jobs so a fresh page can also discover one it never submitted. In `onerror`, do not `close()` on the first failure — leave the browser's reconnect in place while `readyState === EventSource.CONNECTING` and only give up (and clear `currentJob`) after several consecutive failures. Also surface `status === 'queued'` in the stream handler so a job waiting behind another says so.

confirmed.title: Per-image seed offset skips the 63-bit wrap guard, overflowing the SQLite seed column
confirmed.description: `_generate` carefully wraps the per-run base seed at line 197 (`seed = (base + index * req.num_images) % (_MAX_SEED + 1)`, comment: "Wrap rather than overflow the signed 64-bit seed column"), but the per-image seed at line 216 is a bare `seed + offset` with no wrap. `GenerateRequest.seed` is validated `le=2**63-1` and `num_images` up to 8, so `seed + offset` can legally reach `2**63 + 6`. `storage.save_image` writes the PNG to disk (storage.py:140) *before* the INSERT (storage.py:143), and I confirmed SQLite raises `OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to SQLite INTEGER` for any value >= 2**63, while `torch.Generator.manual_seed(2**63)` is accepted — so generation succeeds, the file lands, and only the DB write blows up. `backend/generate.py:320` has the identical defect (`seed=run_seed + offset`).
confirmed.failure_scenario: POST /api/generate with {"prompt":"x","seed":9223372036854775807,"num_images":2} (or `python -m backend.generate "x" --seed 9223372036854775807 --batch 2`). Image 0 saves at seed 2**63-1. Image 1 is generated and written to outputs/ as a PNG, then the INSERT raises OverflowError; the job goes to status "error" with "OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to SQLite INTEGER", every remaining run in the sweep is abandoned, and the second PNG is left on disk as an untracked orphan that only `backend.clear` will ever remove.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Wrap the per-image seed the same way the base seed is wrapped: `seed=(seed + offset) % (_MAX_SEED + 1)` in jobs.py:216 and `seed=(run_seed + offset) % (_MAX_SEED + 1)` in generate.py:320. Ideally also compute the same value for `torch.Generator.manual_seed` in diffusers_backend.py:241 so the recorded seed and the seed actually used stay identical.

confirmed.title: loadGallery() has no in-flight guard, so overlapping calls duplicate one page and skip the next
confirmed.description: `loadGallery()` reads the module-level `offset` when it builds the query (line 326) but only advances it after the await resolves (line 337). Nothing prevents a second call from starting in that window: `els.more.onclick = loadGallery` (line 460) leaves the button enabled during the fetch, and `stepLightbox` awaits `loadGallery()` (line 436) from a keydown handler that fires on OS key repeat. Two overlapping calls issue the same `offset`, both push the returned records into `galleryRecords` and append cards, and then `offset` is advanced twice.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Gallery holds 200 images; page 1 (48) is loaded so offset=48, total=200. Open the lightbox on the last gallery card and hold ArrowRight. keydown #1: next=48 >= lbList.length, canPage() true, `await loadGallery()` starts with offset=48. keydown #2 ~40ms later (key repeat): lbIndex is still 47 and offset is still 48, so canPage() is still true and a second loadGallery() runs with offset=48. Both responses return rows 49-96; galleryRecords becomes 144 entries with 48 duplicates, the grid shows those 48 images twice, offset jumps to 144, and the next 'Load more' fetches rows 145-192 — images 97-144 are never displayed at all, and the lightbox counter (lbIndex+1/lbList.length) is wrong for the rest of the session. A second variant: click 'Load more', then type in the search box; the 250ms-debounced `resetGallery()` clears the grid and `galleryRecords`, and the still-in-flight unfiltered response then appends 48 non-matching images into the filtered view and bumps offset past the filtered page.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Track the in-flight promise and reuse or reject re-entry, e.g. `let galleryPending = null; function loadGallery(){ if (galleryPending) return galleryPending; galleryPending = (async () => { ... })().finally(() => { galleryPending = null; }); return galleryPending; }`, and have `resetGallery()` bump a generation counter that the in-flight call checks before appending its rows.

disputed.title: Clear preview and --dry-run omit orphan PNGs, which are deleted even with --keep-favorites
disputed.description: The number the user confirms against comes only from database rows: `doomed = before["records"] - (favorites if --keep-favorites)` (clear.py:66), printed as "Would delete {doomed} record(s) and their files" (clear.py:81). But `storage.clear_history()` does a second, unconditional pass that unlinks every PNG in outputs_dir with no surviving row (storage.py:263-268). That pass ignores `keep_favorites` entirely and its count never appears in the approval line, nor under `--dry-run` (clear.py:83-85). The orphan count is printed at clear.py:72-73 as a neutral observation ("N of those have no database row"), not as "these will be destroyed". The bail-out at clear.py:76 also needs *both* `records == 0` and `files_on_disk == 0`, so an empty database plus a full outputs folder sails past it.
disputed.failure_scenario: krea.db is deleted, moved, or restored from an older backup while 500 generated PNGs (50 starred) remain in outputs/. `storage._connect()` recreates an empty schema (storage.py:56-63), so all 500 are orphans. The user runs `uv run python -m backend.clear --keep-favorites --dry-run`: it prints "0 records (0 favorite)", "500 PNG files", "Would delete 0 record(s) and their files, keeping 0 favorite(s).", "Dry run - nothing changed." Reassured, they run it for real and type 'clear' - all 500 PNGs including every favorite are unlinked, with the only notice a past-tense "500 orphan(s)" after the fact.
disputed.suggested_fix: Fold orphans into the number being approved and into --dry-run: print "Would delete {doomed} record(s), their files, and {before['orphan_files']} untracked PNG(s) with no database row.", change clear.py:72-73's wording to say they will also be deleted, and give `storage.clear_history()` a `delete_orphans: bool = True` parameter guarding storage.py:263-268 so `--keep-favorites` (or a new `--keep-orphans`) can spare them. Make the clear.py:76 guard bail when nothing at all is scheduled for deletion.

disputed.title: status() calls backend.describe() on the event loop, freezing SSE, cancel and job submission
disputed.description: `async def status()` calls `backend.describe()` directly on the loop thread. `describe()` reaches into CUDA (`torch.cuda.mem_get_info()`, diffusers_backend.py:299), which serializes behind whatever the driver is doing in the loader or generation thread. The project already knows this call is slow - CLAUDE.md says `describe()` "can answer minutes late from behind a load" and app.js:157 repeats it - but the documented mitigation is entirely UI-side (seed defaults once), and nothing addresses the fact that the delay is spent *inside* the loop with nothing else able to run. Every other slow call in main.py is correctly hopped off (`asyncio.to_thread(backend.load)` at :44, `backend.unload` at :116); this one was missed, and `load_model()`/`unload_model()` both re-enter it via `return await status()`.
disputed.failure_scenario: Click Generate on a cold process. The job awaits `ensure_loaded()`, which loads ~13 GB in a worker thread for minutes, while app.js:493 polls `/api/status` every 3 s. Each poll blocks the loop inside `mem_get_info()`. The user clicks Cancel: the POST is accepted by the OS but its handler is never scheduled, so `cancel_requested` is never set and the button sits on "Stopping…". The same stall swallows SSE, so a running sweep's progress bar visibly freezes on every poll.
disputed.suggested_fix: `info = await asyncio.to_thread(backend.describe)` at main.py:90, matching the other two off-loop hops. Optionally memoize the VRAM numbers for ~1 s so the 3 s poll cannot pile work onto the default executor.

disputed.title: --dry-run creates krea.db when it is missing, turning every existing PNG into an orphan
disputed.description: `storage.init_db()` runs at line 63, before the `--dry-run` check at line 83, and `init_db -> _session -> _connect -> sqlite3.connect(settings.db_path)` creates the file when it does not exist. `--dry-run` is documented at clear.py:6 and :59 as "report only, change nothing" and line 84 asserts "nothing changed". The side effect is not cosmetic: the fresh database is empty, so the summary reports 0 records and classifies every PNG in outputs/ as an orphan - and orphans are deleted with no mention in the approval line. A read-only inspection thereby manufactures the exact state in which the tool destroys the whole outputs directory while promising to delete 0 records.
disputed.failure_scenario: The user moves krea.db aside (to keep a backup, or to start a fresh gallery while keeping the images) and runs `uv run python -m backend.clear --dry-run` to see what the tool would touch. The dry run recreates an empty krea.db and prints "0 records ... 40 PNG files ... 40 of those have no database row ... Would delete 0 record(s) and their files. Dry run - nothing changed." They then restore the real krea.db expecting an untouched state, or take the preview at face value and run the real clear, which deletes all 40 images.
disputed.suggested_fix: Do not create a database from a reporting path. Before line 63, if `settings.db_path` does not exist, say so and either exit (dry run) or state plainly that every PNG in outputs/ is untracked and will be deleted. Otherwise move `storage.init_db()` after the dry-run branch and have the report open the database read-only (`sqlite3.connect(f'file:{db_path}?mode=ro', uri=True)`).

unverified.title: An error during deletion loses the report after rows are already committed, and exit 1 collides with abort
unverified.description: Line 100 calls `storage.clear_history()` with no exception handling, and line 101 runs `storage.vacuum()` *before* the result is printed at 103-110. `clear_history` commits the row DELETE first (storage.py:251-253) and only then unlinks files one at a time. Any `OSError` from a single unlink - a PNG held open by the `/outputs` StaticFiles mount, an Explorer preview pane, an antivirus scan - propagates out of `main()` as a bare traceback: the counts are lost, vacuum never runs, and the user cannot tell whether anything was deleted. Because `raise SystemExit(main())` never runs, the process exits 1, the *same* code clear.py returns for "Aborted." (98) and "No confirmation given" (95). A `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked` from the VACUUM suppresses the report the same way, after a fully successful delete.
unverified.failure_scenario: The server is running with the gallery open, so StaticFiles is streaming PNGs from outputs/. The user runs `uv run python -m backend.clear --yes`. One unlink hits WinError 32; the script dies with a traceback and exit 1. The user reads that as "it failed, my gallery is intact" - but every row is already gone and outputs/ holds a partial set of files, all now orphans that the next run will silently delete.
unverified.suggested_fix: Wrap the destructive call and report whatever happened: on `OSError`, print that the rows are already deleted and some files remain, and return a distinct code (2) so partial destruction cannot be confused with the abort path's 1. Move `storage.vacuum()` after the result is printed and give it its own `try/except sqlite3.Error` that warns - a failed shrink must not hide a successful clear.

unverified.title: loadGallery is re-entrant: offset is read before the await and advanced after, duplicating one page and skipping the next
unverified.description: `loadGallery()` snapshots the module-level `offset` into the query string at line 326, awaits the fetch at 330, appends items, and only advances `offset` at 337. Nothing serialises calls and four entry points can overlap: `els.more.onclick = loadGallery` (460, the button is never disabled while the fetch is in flight), `stepLightbox()` (436), the search debounce and favourites checkbox via `resetGallery()` (466-467), and the stream's done handler (283). Two overlapping calls send the same offset, both append the same cards and push the same records into `galleryRecords`, then each add `page.items.length` to `offset`. Duplicated records also break the lightbox strip, since `openLightbox()` resolves position with `list.indexOf(rec)` and always finds the first copy. Cross-filter is worse: `resetGallery()` clears the grid synchronously while an in-flight unfiltered page resolves afterwards into the filtered view, with `total` set by whichever response lands last.
unverified.failure_scenario: With 200 images indexed and one page loaded (offset=48), double-click "Load more". Both requests fetch items 48-95; the grid shows those 48 twice and `offset` becomes 144, so the next "Load more" fetches 144-191 and images 96-143 are unreachable in the grid until a reload. Same root cause via key auto-repeat on ArrowRight at the end of the lightbox strip. Or click "Load more" and immediately tick Favorites - the unfiltered page's cards are appended into the favourites-filtered grid.
unverified.suggested_fix: Guard the pager with an in-flight flag plus a generation token: bump a module-level `galleryEpoch` in `resetGallery()`, capture epoch and offset at the top of `loadGallery()`, and after the await discard the response if the epoch changed; coalesce or bail when a load is already running, clearing the flag in a `finally`. Disable `els.more` for the duration of the request.

unverified.title: A stream error orphans a running job: no reconnect, and Cancel becomes unreachable
unverified.description: `source.onerror` closes the EventSource, calls `setBusy(false)` and shows a banner - and that ends the client's relationship with the job. `setBusy(false)` nulls `currentJob` and disables Cancel, so `cancelJob()` returns immediately and there is no way to stop the job from the UI. The job itself keeps occupying the single-thread GPU pool and keeps writing images. Nothing re-attaches: the job id is not persisted and no code path opens a stream for an existing job. Both sides were built for reattachment - `jobs.events()` deliberately opens with the terminal snapshot "for a stream attached after the fact (a reload...)" and `streamJob` carries the matching replay branch at app.js:276 - but the client half was never written, so the only transport-failure policy is to give up permanently.
unverified.failure_scenario: Start a 64-run 4 MP sweep (hours of GPU time), then interrupt the connection - sleep/resume the machine, or drop WiFi if the server was bound to the LAN. `onerror` fires: banner reads "Lost connection to the generation stream", Generate re-enables, Cancel is disabled, `currentJob` is null. The sweep keeps running for hours writing images that never appear (the gallery is only refreshed from the `done` branch). Clicking Generate submits a second job that blocks on the gate behind the invisible one, so the UI sits on "queued…" indefinitely with no way to cancel either job short of killing the server.
unverified.suggested_fix: Do not treat a transport error as terminal: keep `currentJob` (persist the id in sessionStorage so a reload can resume too) and re-open `new EventSource('/api/jobs/'+id+'/stream')` with bounded backoff, only calling `setBusy(false)` and showing the banner after N failures - the server's opening snapshot plus the existing `!cleared` replay already handle catch-up. Fix the per-subscriber fan-out first, otherwise a reconnect that overlaps the old generator splits the event stream.

unverified.title: max_pixels budgets one image, not the batch, so a valid request asks for 8x the VRAM ceiling
unverified.description: `GenerateRequest.check_budget` - the only guard `generate()` calls - tests `self.width * self.height` alone (schemas.py:34-38). `num_images` is validated independently (`ge=1, le=8`) and never multiplied into the budget, even though CLAUDE.md records that "`num_images` holds the whole batch in VRAM at once" and app.js:116 notes that a single 4 MP image is already the edge of what fits on 16 GB. The accepted request space therefore includes a batch eight times past the documented ceiling, and `DiffusersBackend.generate` passes it straight through as `num_images_per_prompt`.
unverified.failure_scenario: `POST /api/generate {"prompt":"x","width":2368,"height":1776,"num_images":8}` - 4,205,568 <= 4,300,000, so the budget passes and the job is accepted. The pipeline is then asked for eight 4 MP samples at once on top of the ~13 GB resident quantized transformer and raises `torch.OutOfMemoryError` deep in the denoising loop; the job ends in error after the multi-minute model load. This is reachable by clicking, not just by crafting JSON: the UI offers the 4 MP tier and Batch up to 8 in the same form (index.html:51).
unverified.suggested_fix: Add a batch-aware ceiling beside the existing pair (`max_batch_pixels: int = 4_300_000`) and enforce it where the budget is already checked in main.py:126-129, with an error that points at `runs` - the axis CLAUDE.md says costs no extra VRAM - rather than at the size.

unverified.title: Unknown KREA_QUANT/KREA_OFFLOAD values silently pick the heaviest path while status reports the requested value
unverified.description: `_quantization_config()` returns None - full bf16 - for any value outside `("fp8", "int8")` with no log line, and `load()` (137-142) treats any value outside `("model", "sequential")` as "keep everything resident". `config.py:110,115` reads both straight from the environment and never validates them. Line 128 then logs `quant=<the bogus value>` and `describe()` reports `quantization`/`offload` verbatim, so `/api/status` and the UI show the setting as if it were in effect. The CLI guards these with argparse `choices` (generate.py:104-107), but the env vars - the documented way to set them in the README - are unguarded, so the two entry points disagree.
unverified.failure_scenario: `$env:KREA_QUANT = "float8"` (the spelling used in the README requirements line and in this module's own docstring), then `uv run python -m backend.main`. The log prints `quant=float8`, the model loads in bf16 (~24-25 GB), and after several minutes the load dies with CUDA out of memory on a 16 GB card while `/api/status` still reports `quantization: float8`. `KREA_OFFLOAD=cpu` behaves identically: it falls into `pipe.to("cuda")` with everything resident and is reported as `offload: cpu`.
unverified.suggested_fix: Validate in config.py at import time - raise, or clamp with a `log.warning`, when `quantization not in {"fp8","int8","none"}` or `offload not in {"model","sequential","none"}` - and add an explicit `log.warning("quantization %r not recognised; loading in full bf16", ...)` at the fall-through so the log matches what was actually done.

unverified.title: Docs say the default checkpoint is krea/Krea-2-Turbo; config.py defaults to FLUX.1-Krea-dev
unverified.description: `backend/config.py:105` reads `os.getenv("KREA_MODEL_ID", "black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev")`. Commit d826124 touched config.py only, so four documented places now state the opposite default: README.md:132 (settings table, `| KREA_MODEL_ID | krea/Krea-2-Turbo |`), README.md:3 ("Run **Krea 2 Turbo** locally"), README.md:39-43 ("While you wait, FLUX.1 Krea [dev] runs through the same app: `$env:KREA_MODEL_ID = ...`" - now a no-op, and the *Krea* id is the one that must be set), and CLAUDE.md:3. The stale comment at config.py:101 ("Krea 2 Turbo is the 8-step distilled variant") sits directly above the FLUX default and reinforces the wrong reading.
unverified.failure_scenario: A user follows README "One-time setup": requests manual approval for krea/Krea-2-Turbo, gets it, does not click through the FLUX gate (the README frames FLUX as the fallback only "while you wait"), then runs the server and hits Generate. The backend loads FLUX.1-Krea-dev and the first generate fails with a gated-repo 403 for a repo the README never told them to request. If they do have FLUX access, they silently get FLUX output while README:3 and the status text tell them they are running the 8-step Turbo model.
unverified.suggested_fix: Set README.md:132 to `black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev` and move `krea/Krea-2-Turbo` into the Notes column, rewrite README.md:3 and :39-43 so the click-through gate is the default path and `$env:KREA_MODEL_ID = "krea/Krea-2-Turbo"` is the opt-in, amend CLAUDE.md:3, and fix the stale comment at backend/config.py:101.

unverified.title: Sticky control panel has no max-height, so Generate, progress and Cancel can be unreachable
unverified.description: `.panel` is `position: sticky; top: 68px` with no `max-height` and no `overflow`. When the panel is taller than the viewport, sticky pins its top for the whole scroll length of `main`, so everything below the fold - the Generate button (index.html:57), the progress row with Cancel (58-62) and the error line (63) - stays off-screen and cannot be scrolled to while the gallery is long. Growing the panel past the viewport is routine: `textarea` is `resize: vertical`, so dragging the prompt box taller for a long prompt is normal, and the panel also grows by the progress row and an error line during a run.
unverified.failure_scenario: On a 768 px-tall laptop with a full gallery loaded, drag the prompt textarea taller so the panel exceeds the window. Scroll down to look at earlier results, then try to start the run: the panel's top stays pinned at 68 px and Generate never comes back into view. The only escape is scrolling to the very bottom of the entire gallery or shrinking the textarea. The same trap hides Cancel mid-run, which is the one time-sensitive control.
unverified.suggested_fix: Constrain and scroll the sticky panel: `.panel { max-height: calc(100vh - 86px); overflow-y: auto; }`, and drop sticky positioning inside the `max-width: 900px` media query where the single-column layout gives it no travel anyway.

unverified.title: Gallery card buttons are focusable but rendered at opacity 0 unless hovered, including Delete
unverified.description: `.card .tools` is `opacity: 0` (223) and revealed only by `.card:hover .tools` (225). The three buttons inside it - Reuse, Favorite, Delete (app.js:360-373) - are real `<button>` elements, so they stay in the tab order and stay clickable while fully transparent. There is no `:focus-within` or `:focus-visible` rule anywhere in the stylesheet, and `opacity` applies to the whole rendered subtree including the UA focus ring, so a focused button in the grid is completely invisible. A full page of 48 cards puts 144 invisible tab stops between the search box and "Load more", and the Delete handler has no confirmation step.
unverified.failure_scenario: Load the page with a populated gallery, click into Search, then press Tab three times. Focus is on the first card's Delete button but nothing on screen has changed. Pressing Enter fires `DELETE /api/images/{id}`: an image is permanently removed from disk and the index, the card vanishes from a part of the page the user was not looking at, and no confirmation was shown.
unverified.suggested_fix: Reveal the tools on keyboard focus as well as hover - `.card:hover .tools, .card:focus-within .tools { opacity: 1; }` - and add `.card .tools button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent-2); outline-offset: 1px; }`. Consider a confirm step or an undo on Delete.

unverified.title: Quantized load path rejects local checkpoint directories
unverified.description: `_component_libraries()` always resolves model_index.json through `hf_hub_download(model_id, ...)`, which validates `model_id` as a Hub repo id via `@validate_hf_hub_args`. `DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained` has no such restriction - it branches on `os.path.isdir(...)` and uses a local folder as-is - but `_quantization_config()` runs at line 130, before the loader ever sees the directory, so a local path dies first. CLAUDE.md's "the loader is model-agnostic" note is exactly the claim this breaks; `--quant none` skips `_component_libraries` entirely and loads the same directory fine.
unverified.failure_scenario: `uv run python -m backend.generate "a fox" --model C:\models\krea2-diffusers` (or the same value in `KREA_MODEL_ID`) with the default `KREA_QUANT=fp8` aborts immediately with `HFValidationError: Repo id must use alphanumeric chars, '-', '_' or '.' ... : 'C:\models\krea2-diffusers'`, an error that points at the model id rather than at quantization.
unverified.suggested_fix: Read the index locally when the id is a directory: `path = os.path.join(model_id, "model_index.json") if os.path.isdir(model_id) else hf_hub_download(model_id, "model_index.json")`, then open that path.

unverified.title: One destructive asyncio.Queue per job, but /stream accepts any number of readers
unverified.description: `Job.queue` is a single `asyncio.Queue` consumed destructively at jobs.py:244, and `_emit` does one `put_nowait` per event. `GET /api/jobs/{job_id}/stream` places no limit on how many clients attach to the same job, so N concurrent streams race for the events rather than each receiving them - every `progress`, `image` and `done` goes to exactly one reader. `_finish`'s `done_sent` guard makes it worse: exactly one `done` is ever queued, so a second reader can never be satisfied.
unverified.failure_scenario: With a job streaming to the browser, run `curl -N http://127.0.0.1:7860/api/jobs/<id>/stream` in a terminal (or open the URL in a second tab). The two readers split the events: roughly half the `image` events never reach the browser and the progress bar freezes at whatever step curl swallowed. If curl wins the final `done`, the browser's handler never runs `source.close()`/`setBusy(false)`, so Generate stays disabled reading "Generating…" and the page is stuck until reloaded.
unverified.suggested_fix: Fan out instead of sharing one queue: give `Job` a `subscribers: list[asyncio.Queue]`, have `events()` create its own queue and remove it in a `finally`, and make `_emit` iterate the list. An append-only `job.events` list plus an `asyncio.Event` is equally small and additionally lets a reattached stream replay from its own cursor, which the reconnect fix needs.

unverified.title: Per-image seed is added after the modulo, so a near-max seed overflows the SQLite column
unverified.description: Both sweep loops wrap the *run* seed but not the *per-image* seed. generate.py:296 computes `run_seed = (seed + index * num_images) % (_MAX_SEED + 1)` with the comment "Wrap rather than overflow the signed 64-bit seed column", then line 320 passes `seed=run_seed + offset`; jobs.py:197/216 do exactly the same. Because `offset` runs 0..num_images-1 *after* the modulo, the value handed to storage can reach `_MAX_SEED + 7`, i.e. >= 2**63 - precisely the overflow the wrap was written to prevent. `GenerateRequest.seed` accepts `le=2**63-1`, and `torch.Generator.manual_seed` takes 2**63 happily, so generation succeeds and the PNG is written before the INSERT raises. This is not drift between the two copies - they agree line for line, as CLAUDE.md claims - so the fix has to land in both.
unverified.failure_scenario: `uv run python -m backend.generate "a lighthouse" --seed 9223372036854775807 --batch 2`. Offset 0 saves normally; offset 1 makes seed 9223372036854775808, the PNG is written to outputs/, then the INSERT raises `OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to SQLite INTEGER`, the sweep aborts and exits 1, leaving an untracked PNG that only a later `backend.clear` orphan sweep will remove. The same request through POST /api/generate ends the job in status "error" after one image.
unverified.suggested_fix: Move the wrap to the value actually stored and seeded, in both files: `image_seed = (run_seed + offset) % (_MAX_SEED + 1)` inside the enumerate loop, matched by the same wrap where the generator is built (diffusers_backend.py:241), or clamp the accepted base seed so `seed + num_images - 1` cannot exceed _MAX_SEED.

unverified.title: save_image never recreates outputs_dir, so a removed folder breaks generation until restart
unverified.description: `settings.outputs_dir` is created exactly once, at import of config.py (line 137), and never again. `save_image` calls `image.save(path, ...)` at line 140 with no check that the parent still exists. This is the exact failure class the same module already self-heals for the database: `_connect()` carries a comment (56-59) about the file disappearing under a running server and re-runs the schema. Nothing else notices the missing directory either - `glob("*.png")` on a missing directory returns empty, so `summarise()` reports `files_on_disk: 0` and `clear_history()` reports success while every generation is failing.
unverified.failure_scenario: The user deletes or renames outputs/ to reclaim disk space (or right after a `backend.clear` run leaves it empty) while the server is up, then submits a prompt. The model loads, the full denoising pass runs, and it dies in `save_image` with `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '...\\outputs\\20260829-143012-42-a3f9c1.png'`. The image is discarded, no row is written, and every subsequent job fails identically for the life of the process.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add `settings.outputs_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` immediately before the `image.save(...)` call (a cheap stat on the happy path), mirroring the schema-recovery check `_connect()` already performs per connection.

unverified.title: delete_image commits the row deletion before an unguarded unlink, so a locked file 500s with the record already gone
unverified.description: `delete_image` deletes the row inside `_session()` (216-217), which commits on exit, and only then unlinks the file. `missing_ok=True` covers a vanished file but not a locked one: on Windows, unlinking a file another process holds open raises `PermissionError [WinError 32]`, which escapes `delete_image` and turns `DELETE /api/images/{id}` into a 500 - after the row is permanently committed as deleted. There is no compensating re-insert and no try/finally.
unverified.failure_scenario: The user has outputs/ open in Explorer with the preview pane showing a 2K PNG (or any viewer/AV scanner holding the handle) and clicks the delete tool on that card. `unlink` raises, the endpoint returns 500, and the card's async click handler (app.js:363-372) has no catch, so `div.remove()` never runs and the card silently stays on screen with no error shown. Clicking delete again returns 404 "unknown image" because the row went in the first call, and the PNG is left on disk as an orphan.
unverified.suggested_fix: Unlink first and delete the row only once the file is gone, or keep the order but wrap the unlink in `try/except OSError`, log it, and still return success - the DB is the source of truth for the gallery and the orphan sweep already handles a leftover file.

unverified.title: A fully completed sweep is reported as cancelled when the cancel lands after the last image
unverified.description: Line 161 derives the terminal status purely from the flag: `job.status = "cancelled" if job.cancel_requested else "done"`. It never asks whether `_generate` actually stopped early. `_generate` only breaks on `cancel_requested` at the top of a run (192) or on `Cancelled` from the backend (206); if it ran all `req.runs` passes and returned normally, every image is saved. But `_run` resumes from `run_in_executor` on a later loop iteration, and the cancel endpoint runs on that same loop, so a cancel POST scheduled after the worker's future resolved but before `_run` wakes still sets the flag and mislabels a complete run.
unverified.failure_scenario: Run a 4-run sweep. The last image appears in the browser and the user clicks Cancel on the very next tick. `cancel()` sees status still "running" and sets `cancel_requested`. `_run` wakes and marks the job "cancelled" although all 4 runs completed, so the terminal SSE event makes app.js show "Cancelled — kept 4 images." for a sweep that finished in full, and `GET /api/jobs/{id}` records it as cancelled permanently.
unverified.suggested_fix: Have `_generate` report whether it stopped early rather than re-deriving it from the flag - return True from the two break paths and the `Cancelled` handler, False on normal completion - then `job.status = "cancelled" if interrupted else "done"`.

unverified.title: _run overwrites a terminal status after the done event was already sent for a cancelled job
unverified.description: `cancel()` finishes a still-queued job on the spot: status becomes "cancelled", `done_sent` is set and the terminal SSE event goes out. But the job's `_run` task is at that moment parked in `await self._ensure_loaded()` (144), *before* the `cancel_requested` check inside the gate at 153. If the load then fails, the except at 145-148 unconditionally rewrites `job.status = "error"` and `job.error`. `_finish()` correctly refuses a second done event, so the stream stays consistent - but the job object does not; there is no `if job.status in _TERMINAL: return` guard on this path.
unverified.failure_scenario: Cold process, no HF token for a gated repo. Click Generate; the job parks on `ensure_loaded()`. Click Cancel a second later: the job is marked cancelled, the SSE done arrives and the UI shows "Cancelled before anything finished." Three minutes later the load fails with a 403; `_run` resumes and rewrites the job to `status="error"`. `GET /api/jobs/{id}` now reports error for a job the user was told was cancelled, and a stream reattached to that id replays a load error the user already dismissed by cancelling.
unverified.suggested_fix: Guard the resume path on the already-terminal state - `if job.status in _TERMINAL: return` right after `await self._ensure_loaded()` returns or raises - and inside the except only set status/error when `not job.done_sent`.

unverified.title: The per-run status event ships the whole accumulated images array, which the client discards
unverified.description: The status event emitted at the top of every run uses `**job.snapshot()`, and `snapshot()` includes `"images": self.images` - every ImageRecord produced so far, each carrying its own copy of the prompt (up to 4000 chars) and negative prompt. The payload grows linearly per run, so the total shipped is quadratic in run count. The client reads nothing from it: the status branch at app.js:269-271 touches only `data.run` and `data.total_runs`. The `done` snapshot (136) and the opening snapshot (240) genuinely need `images`; this one does not.
unverified.failure_scenario: runs=64, num_images=8 with a 300-character prompt: the run-64 status event carries 504 records, and the sweep pushes ~16,000 redundant records (roughly 11 MB, far more at the 4000-char prompt limit) through the SSE socket, all json.dumps'd on the event loop in main.py:162 and then thrown away. Nothing breaks, but every run boundary adds an avoidable serialization stall to the loop that also serves the 3-second /api/status poll.
unverified.suggested_fix: Emit the run marker without the gallery - an explicit dict of `status`/`job_id`/`run`/`total_runs`/`step`/`total_steps`, or a `snapshot(include_images=False)` flag - and leave `_finish` and the opening event on the full snapshot, since the client's catch-up replay depends on them.

unverified.title: settings.device is ignored on both offload paths
unverified.description: `enable_model_cpu_offload()` and `enable_sequential_cpu_offload()` are called with no `device` argument, so diffusers resolves the target itself and defaults to the first available accelerator. `settings.device` therefore only takes effect in the `offload == "none"` branch at line 142 - i.e. never on the default configuration. The explicit CUDA-availability guard at line 123 shows non-cuda values are meant to be usable, and `describe()` reports `get_device_name(0)` unconditionally, so nothing surfaces the mismatch.
unverified.failure_scenario: On a two-GPU box, `$env:KREA_DEVICE = "cuda:1"` with the default `KREA_OFFLOAD=model`: the weights are offloaded to cuda:0, contending with whatever already occupies GPU 0, and /api/status names GPU 0 as the device, so nothing indicates the setting was dropped.
unverified.suggested_fix: Pass the configured device through - `pipe.enable_model_cpu_offload(device=settings.device)` / `pipe.enable_sequential_cpu_offload(device=settings.device)` - and short-circuit to `pipe.to(settings.device)` when the configured device is not an accelerator.

unverified.title: collect() sends negative_prompt even at CFG <= 1, so records claim a prompt that was never used
unverified.description: `syncCfg()` disables the negative textarea when CFG <= 1, correctly signalling it has no effect - but a disabled textarea still reports its value, and `collect()` reads `els.negative.value` unconditionally, so the text is sent anyway. `DiffusersBackend.generate` then drops it, while `storage.save_image` writes `request.negative_prompt` into the images row and into the PNG's A1111 `parameters`/`krea` metadata as if it had been applied. CLAUDE.md documents dropping the negative prompt from the *pipeline call*; it says nothing about recording one that was ignored, and `ImageRecord.negative_prompt` is part of what Reuse restores.
unverified.failure_scenario: On FLUX the profile seeds CFG 3.5, so the negative box is enabled. Type "blurry, watermark", set CFG to 0 for a fast draft - the box greys out but keeps its text - and Generate. The saved row and the PNG both record `Negative prompt: blurry, watermark` for an image that never saw it; later, Reuse on that record loads it back and at any CFG > 1 produces a visibly different image than the record implies.
unverified.suggested_fix: Mirror the backend's rule in `collect()`: read the CFG value first and send `negative_prompt: cfg > <threshold> ? (els.negative.value.trim() || null) : null`, so what is recorded is what was actually used.

unverified.title: collect() coerces cleared number inputs to 0, producing a raw pydantic 422 blob
unverified.description: `collect()` uses bare `+els.<x>.value` for width, height, steps, guidance_scale, num_images and runs. `<input type="number">` reports `''` when cleared and `+'' === 0`; none of the inputs is `required` or inside a `<form>`, so nothing blocks submission. `syncRuns()` already normalises the same fields for its hint text (`Math.max(1, +els.runs.value || 1)`), so the hint and the payload disagree. The resulting 422's `detail` is a list of dicts, and `api()` falls through to `JSON.stringify(detail)`, so the error slot shows a wall of raw JSON. `guidance_scale` is the worse case: 0 is inside `ge=0.0`, so a cleared CFG box is accepted and silently changes the run.
unverified.failure_scenario: Click into the Batch box, press Backspace to clear it (the run hint still reads as if batch were 1), then click Generate. The payload carries `num_images: 0` and the panel shows `[{"type":"greater_than_equal","loc":["body","num_images"],"msg":"Input should be greater than or equal to 1",...}]` instead of generating. Clearing CFG instead silently submits guidance_scale 0.
unverified.suggested_fix: Normalise in `collect()` the way `syncRuns()` already does (a small `num(el, fallback)` helper that rejects empty strings), and teach `api()` to flatten a list-shaped `detail` into `detail.map(e => \`${e.loc.slice(1).join('.')}: ${e.msg}\`).join('; ')` so any remaining validation error is readable.

unverified.title: Lightbox opens without moving, trapping or restoring focus and has no dialog semantics
unverified.description:
`renderLightbox()` opens the overlay by clearing the `hidden` attribute and nothing else. It is opened by clicking a non-focusable ``, so the click leaves focus on ``; the code never focuses anything inside the overlay, never records `document.activeElement` to restore in `closeLightbox()`, never traps Tab, and never marks the page behind it inert or aria-hidden. The container is a plain `
` with no `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal`, so assistive tech does not report a modal at all.
unverified.failure_scenario: Click a gallery thumbnail to open the lightbox, then press Tab. Focus was on `<body>`, so Tab moves to the first tabbable element in DOM order - `#btn-unload` in the topbar - which is hidden behind the full-screen overlay. Pressing Enter there calls `POST /api/model/unload`: the checkpoint is dropped from VRAM with no visible cause and the next Generate silently re-triggers a multi-minute load. Continuing to Tab walks the entire invisible panel before reaching the lightbox's own buttons, which are last in the document.
unverified.suggested_fix: In `openLightbox`, save `document.activeElement`, give the overlay `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` (or convert it to a `<dialog>` and use `showModal()`, which gives the trap and Escape for free), focus `#lb-close` after unhiding, keep Tab inside the overlay, and restore the saved element in `closeLightbox()`.

unverified.title: Images are the only trigger for the lightbox and are not keyboard-reachable
unverified.description: Both entry points into the lightbox are `img.onclick` handlers on bare `` elements - the viewer (312) and the gallery cards (349). `` is not focusable and neither element gets `tabindex`, `role="button"` or a keydown handler, so there is no keyboard path into the lightbox at all. That matters beyond zooming: a just-generated image has no tools row in the viewer, and its only "Reuse settings" control is `#lb-reuse` inside the lightbox.
unverified.failure_scenario: A keyboard-only user generates an image and tabs through the page: Unload, prompt, negative, the numeric fields, dice, Generate, search, Favorites, the (invisible) card buttons, Load more - the viewer image is skipped entirely. No key press opens the lightbox, so the fresh image can never be viewed full size, never walked with the arrow handlers, and its settings can never be loaded back into the panel; the user has to retype prompt, size, steps, CFG, mu and seed by hand.
unverified.suggested_fix: Make the thumbnails real controls: wrap each `` in a `

unverified.title: Progress, status and error text update silently - no live region and no progressbar semantics
unverified.description: `#progress-text` (60), `#status-text` (14) and `#error` (63) are all rewritten from JS - step counts on every SSE progress event, the model state every 3 s, and `showError` revealing the paragraph by clearing `hidden` - and none carries `aria-live`, `role="status"` or `role="alert"`; there is no ARIA attribute anywhere in web/. The progress bar itself (`.bar`/`.fill`) is two styled divs with no `role="progressbar"` and no `aria-valuenow`, so its width animation conveys nothing non-visually.
unverified.failure_scenario: A screen-reader user presses Generate. The button label flips to "Generating…" and the progress row appears, but nothing is announced; minutes pass with no output while the model loads and denoises. If the run then fails - a 4 MP batch raising CUDA out-of-memory - `showError(data.error)` reveals the message in a paragraph with no live region, so the user hears nothing at all: the button quietly returns to "Generate" and no images appear, with no announced explanation. The "Cancelled — kept N images." note is equally silent.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add `role="status" aria-live="polite"` to `#progress-text` and `#status-text`, `role="alert"` to `#error`, and `role="progressbar" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="100"` to `.bar`, updating `aria-valuenow` alongside `els.fill.style.width` in `streamJob`.

unverified.title: Icon-only buttons are named by punctuation glyphs; their title is ignored for the accessible name
unverified.description: `tool(label, title, onClick)` sets `b.textContent = label` and `b.title = title`. For a `<button>`, accessible-name computation takes text content ahead of `title`, so `title` never becomes the name - it is only a mouse tooltip. The gallery buttons are therefore named `↻`, `☆`/`★` and `⌦`, which screen readers announce as nothing or as a raw code point. The same pattern appears on the static buttons: `#btn-dice` is 🎲 (announced "game die", not "clear seed"), `#lb-close` is ✕, and `#lb-prev`/`#lb-next` are ‹/› which are punctuation and normally not spoken.
unverified.failure_scenario: A screen-reader user tabs through the gallery grid. Each card presents three controls announced as "button", "button", "button" with no distinguishing name, one of which permanently deletes the image; the user cannot tell Reuse from Favorite from Delete except by activating one. In the lightbox, Prev/Next are unnamed buttons, so paging through results is guesswork.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add `b.setAttribute('aria-label', title)` inside `tool()` (aria-label outranks content), wrap the glyph in `<span aria-hidden="true">`, and add explicit `aria-label` attributes to `#btn-dice`, `#lb-close`, `#lb-prev` and `#lb-next` in index.html.

unverified.title: stepLightbox applies an index computed before its await, so a back-step during page load jumps forward
unverified.description: `stepLightbox()` computes `const next = lbIndex + delta` at line 431, then may `await loadGallery()` at 436 before assigning `lbIndex = next` at 439. `lbIndex` can be changed by any call that runs during that await - the handler is re-entrant and nothing re-derives `next` afterwards, so the stale index wins. The only bound rechecked after the await is `next >= lbList.length`.
unverified.failure_scenario: Lightbox open on the last loaded gallery image (index 47 of 48, total 200). Press ArrowRight - `next` is 48 and the handler suspends in `await loadGallery()`. Before the page lands, press ArrowLeft: that call runs synchronously, setting `lbIndex = 46` and rendering image 46. The pending call then resumes and executes `lbIndex = 48; renderLightbox()`, dropping the user who just asked to go back onto image 48.
unverified.suggested_fix: Re-derive the target after the await: record `const from = lbIndex` before it and bail if `lbIndex !== from` on resume, or recompute `lbIndex + delta` post-await and re-check the bounds. The in-flight guard on `loadGallery` removes the overlap that makes this reachable.

unverified.title: The lightbox image keeps alt="" forever, so the full-size view is exposed as decorative
unverified.description: `renderLightbox()` assigns `els.lbImg.src = rec.url` but never touches `alt`, and the markup hardcodes `` (index.html:85). An empty alt is the explicit signal "this image is decorative, skip it", so the largest and most important image on the page is removed from the accessibility tree - while the identical image in the viewer and in the gallery cards does set `img.alt = rec.prompt`.
unverified.failure_scenario: A screen-reader user opens an image in the lightbox and walks the overlay: the image is skipped silently as decorative, so the announced content is just the buttons and the metadata line. Opening a second image changes `src` but the empty alt persists, so consecutive images are indistinguishable to anything reading the DOM.
unverified.suggested_fix: Set the alt alongside the src in `renderLightbox`: `els.lbImg.alt = rec.prompt;`, and clear it in `closeLightbox()` where `src` is cleared.

unverified.title: The "(needs CFG > 1)" hint sits at ~3.0:1 contrast, below AA for 12px text
unverified.description: `.field em { ... opacity: 0.65 }` applies to `#neg-note`, which inherits `color: var(--muted)` (#8b8b9a) and `font-size: 12px` from `.field > span`. Composited at 65% over the panel background #131318 the effective colour is about #61616d, roughly 3.0:1 - below the 4.5:1 AA threshold for text this size. This is not only a disabled state: the note renders at that opacity whenever the field is shown, including with CFG at 3.5 on FLUX where the negative prompt is fully active.
unverified.failure_scenario: On a bright screen or a laptop panel viewed off-axis, "(needs CFG > 1 — ~2× slower)" is illegible next to the Negative prompt label. A user types a negative prompt with CFG at Turbo's default of 0, cannot read the one piece of text explaining why the box is greyed out, and concludes the negative prompt is broken.
unverified.suggested_fix: Drop the `opacity` and express the de-emphasis in colour instead - `var(--muted)` alone against `--panel` is about 5.5:1 and still reads as secondary. (Same file, related near-miss: `.primary` is #fff on `--accent` #7c5cff at about 4.16:1.)

unverified.title: --mu and --no-mu are not mutually exclusive; --no-mu silently discards an explicit --mu
unverified.description: `mu = None if args.no_mu else (args.mu if args.mu is not None else profile["mu"])` gives `--no-mu` unconditional priority. Both flags live in the same `sampling` group and neither is in an `add_mutually_exclusive_group`, so passing both is accepted and the explicitly requested mu is dropped with no message. That is inconsistent with the file's own handling of the other conflicting pair: `_resolve_size` calls `parser.error("--width/--height and --aspect/--mp are alternatives; pick one")`. mu is part of the reproduction set (persisted in ImageRecord and PNG metadata) and on Turbo a different mu is a different image.
unverified.failure_scenario: `uv run python -m backend.generate "..." --mu 2.0 --no-mu` (a scripted sweep that always appends --no-mu, or a shell-history edit that leaves the old flag in place). The summary prints `sampling : 8 steps, CFG 0.0, mu -`, no warning is emitted, exit code is 0, and the saved PNG and gallery row record mu=null - a different image from the one requested.
unverified.suggested_fix: Declare them as alternatives, mirroring the size flags: put `--mu` and `--no-mu` in `sampling.add_mutually_exclusive_group()`, or add `if args.mu is not None and args.no_mu: parser.error("--mu and --no-mu are alternatives; pick one")` next to the existing size check.

unverified.title: Ctrl-C during the weight load prints a step-cancel message but cannot stop the load
unverified.description: The SIGINT handler is installed at line 255, before `backend.load()` at 261. It only sets `stop = True` and prints "cancelling at the end of this step (Ctrl-C again to force)...". During the load there are no denoising steps and nothing polls `stop` - `DiffusersBackend.load()` has no cancellation hook - so the load runs to completion, which the CLI's own message at 258 describes as "minutes on a cold cache". Only when it returns does the sweep loop hit `if stop: break` and exit having generated nothing, so the message is wrong about both what will happen and when, and the docstring's "Ctrl-C stops at the end of the current step" does not hold for the load phase.
unverified.failure_scenario: `uv run python -m backend.generate "..."` on a cold HF cache; the user hits Ctrl-C 20 seconds in after spotting a typo in the prompt. The CLI prints the step-cancel message and then keeps downloading and loading weights for several more minutes, finally printing "ready in 4m12s" followed by "0/1 image(s) in 4m12s." and exiting 130. The user has to guess that a second Ctrl-C is what actually aborts.
unverified.suggested_fix: Track the phase - set a `loading = True` flag around the `backend.load()` call - and have `_on_sigint` either print a phase-appropriate message ("weights are still loading; Ctrl-C again to abort now") or raise KeyboardInterrupt immediately while loading, which the existing `except KeyboardInterrupt` at 262 already handles cleanly with exit 130.

unverified.title: README promises --quiet emits bare paths; generate.py appends "  seed N" to every line
unverified.description: README.md:83-84 says "`--quiet` prints only the paths of the images it saved, one per line, so a shell can consume them." generate.py:325-327 prints unconditionally, quiet or not: `print(f"{p.settings.outputs_dir / record.filename}  seed {record.seed}", flush=True)`. Every line is `<path>  seed <n>`, never a bare path. `--quiet` only suppresses the header block and the closing summary; generate.py:237 also prints "Dry run - nothing generated." under `--quiet`, so `--dry-run --quiet` emits a line that is neither a path nor the settings.
unverified.failure_scenario: `uv run python -m backend.generate "a lighthouse" --runs 4 --quiet | while read -r p; do magick "$p" -resize 50% thumb.png; done` - the line is `C:\...\20260829-101500-42-a1b2c3.png  seed 42`, so word-splitting hands the consumer a path plus the literal tokens `seed` and `42` and the loop fails (or, unquoted, processes the wrong argument list). Anything piping --quiet output into xargs or read is broken by the suffix.
unverified.suggested_fix: Make the code match the doc - `print(path if args.quiet else f"{path}  seed {record.seed}")` at generate.py:325 and skip the "Dry run" line under `--quiet` - since the doc's stated purpose is shell consumption. Otherwise correct README.md:83-84.

unverified.title: CLAUDE.md claims all config.py settings are KREA_* overridable; five fields read no environment
unverified.description: CLAUDE.md:17 states "`backend/config.py` — settings, all overridable by `KREA_*` env vars". Only 7 of the 12 `Settings` fields call `os.getenv`/`_env_bool`. The remaining five are hardcoded literals with no environment hook: `outputs_dir`, `db_path`, `web_dir`, `max_side` and `max_pixels`. There is no `KREA_OUTPUTS_DIR`, `KREA_DB_PATH`, `KREA_MAX_SIDE` or `KREA_MAX_PIXELS` anywhere in the codebase.
unverified.failure_scenario: Wanting a 64-image overnight sweep written to a data drive rather than the repo, a user (or an agent acting on CLAUDE.md) runs `$env:KREA_OUTPUTS_DIR = "D:\renders"; uv run python -m backend.generate "..." --runs 64 --mp 4`. The variable is ignored, 64 PNGs land inside the git working tree, and the CLI's printed `output : ... -> <ROOT>\outputs` line is the only clue anything was disregarded. Same silent no-op for raising the pixel budget via the environment before hitting the 422.
unverified.suggested_fix: Narrow the claim in CLAUDE.md to the fields that are actually environment-backed (model/quant/offload/device/preload/host/port) and name the paths and size guard rails as compile-time constants - or, if the broader claim is the intent, add the missing `os.getenv` lookups in config.py.

unverified.title: Settings table omits KREA_HOST and KREA_DEVICE, which config.py does read
unverified.description: README.md:128 introduces the table as "All optional, set as environment variables", then lists five variables. config.py reads two more that are absent: `KREA_DEVICE` (line 117, default "cuda", consumed by diffusers_backend.py:123 and :142) and `KREA_HOST` (line 124, default "127.0.0.1", consumed by main.py:205). The table presents itself as the complete settings surface, so both look unsupported.
unverified.failure_scenario: A user wants to reach the UI from a laptop on the same LAN. The table lists only KREA_PORT, so they conclude the bind address is not configurable and either edit config.py by hand or set up a reverse proxy - when `$env:KREA_HOST = "0.0.0.0"` already works. Similarly, someone debugging on a machine with no CUDA has no documented route to the KREA_DEVICE escape hatch the backend checks before raising "CUDA is not available to PyTorch".
unverified.suggested_fix: Add two rows: `| KREA_HOST | 127.0.0.1 | 0.0.0.0 to expose the server on the LAN |` and `| KREA_DEVICE | cuda | |`.

unverified.title: CLAUDE.md Layout map omits backend/clear.py and backend/model_defaults.py
unverified.description: The Layout section (17-25) maps every backend module one per line and ends at `backend/generate.py` and `web/`. Two modules that exist are missing: `backend/clear.py` (a 115-line user-facing CLI, documented under README's "Clearing history" and owning `storage.clear_history`/`vacuum`) and `backend/model_defaults.py` (discussed later at CLAUDE.md:52-57 and imported by main.py:17 and generate.py:149, but never placed in the map).
unverified.failure_scenario: An agent or new contributor asked to add an `--older-than 7d` history purge reads the Layout list to find the owning module, sees only config/schemas/backends/jobs/storage/main/generate, and adds a deletion path to main.py or a fresh script - duplicating the confirmation, orphan-sweep and vacuum logic clear.py and storage.py already implement, and diverging from the documented `uv run python -m backend.clear` interface.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add to the Layout list: "- `backend/model_defaults.py` — recommended steps/CFG/mu per checkpoint id" and "- `backend/clear.py` — CLI to delete generated images and their history".

unverified.title: The SIZES preset table is maintained twice, in generate.py and web/app.js, with config.py's budget derived by hand
unverified.description: `SIZES`/`TIERS` (generate.py:45-52) is a verbatim second copy of `SIZES`/`TIERS` in web/app.js:26-34 - the comment on line 42 even says "kept in step with it", which is the problem rather than the mitigation. CLAUDE.md defends the *sweep-loop* duplication in generate.py ("a dozen lines" of seed maths) and enumerates what must not drift; this 15-entry lookup table is neither covered by that argument nor welded to a Job - it is pure data with an obvious home. A third derived copy sits in config.py:132-133, where `max_side` and `max_pixels` are tied to the largest preset only by a prose comment.
unverified.failure_scenario: A UI change touches web/app.js alone - say 4 MP at 1:1 becomes 2160x2160, or a 6 MP tier is added. `python -m backend.generate --mp 4` still emits 2048x2048, so re-running a gallery image's recorded settings through the CLI no longer reproduces it, breaking the module docstring's promise that a CLI image is identical to the browser's. With a 6 MP tier the divergence is louder: the button posts 2880x2880 and `check_budget()` rejects the UI's own preset with a 422 against the untouched max_pixels.
unverified.suggested_fix: Move the table into one `backend/sizes.py`; import it in generate.py, derive `max_side`/`max_pixels` from it in config.py, and serve it (in `/api/status`, which the page already fetches at startup, or a two-line `/api/sizes`) so `buildPresets()` builds the rows from the response instead of its own literal.

unverified.title: DiffusersBackend._error is write-only state; describe()'s detail/backend/pipeline keys are read by nobody
unverified.description: `self._error` is assigned None in `__init__` (44) and None again at the end of `load()` (156), and is never assigned a message anywhere in the tree - a failing load raises straight out of `load()` and is recorded by `main.ensure_loaded()` in `_load_state`. Its only read is `describe()["detail"]` (292), and `main.status()` ignores that key entirely, taking `detail=_load_state["detail"]` (main.py:100). The `"backend"` and `"pipeline"` keys have no reader either. So the file carries an error channel that can never carry an error, wired to a consumer that would not read it.
unverified.failure_scenario: Someone follows the ABC docstring ("Backend/device metadata for the status endpoint") when adding the ComfyUI backend CLAUDE.md invites, sets `describe()["detail"] = "comfy: connection refused"` on a failed connect, and the message never reaches the browser: `/api/status` overwrites `detail` with `_load_state["detail"]`, which is None whenever the failure did not come out of `backend.load()`. The dead `_error` field is what makes that look like a supported path.
unverified.suggested_fix: Delete `self._error` and the unread `detail`/`backend`/`pipeline` keys - or, if a per-backend detail is wanted, have `main.status()` fall back to `info.get("detail")` when `_load_state["detail"]` is None and actually set `_error` in the load failure path.

unverified.title: The 'mu' column read guard defends a database shape this project has never written, and its comment is wrong
unverified.description: `mu=row["mu"] if "mu" in row.keys() else None` is justified by the comment "Databases written before mu was indexed have no such column". Git history contradicts it: `mu REAL` has been in `_SCHEMA` since f1d7ccc, the commit that first added the app (confirmed with `git show f1d7ccc:backend/storage.py`), while the guard itself only arrived in 2922c44 - which actually fixed `ImageRecord` not *serving* mu, exactly as schemas.py:51-52 says. No database this code has created lacks the column, and one that did would fail on the very next `save_image()` anyway, since the INSERT names `mu` unconditionally.
unverified.failure_scenario: No runtime failure; the cost is a false invariant. The comment tells the next maintainer that legacy schemas without `mu` are in circulation and must be tolerated on read, inviting the same defensive `in row.keys()` dance for the next added column - each of which would in fact break the write path outright, since there is no migration step. The guard also builds a 13-element key list per row, 48 rows per gallery page.
unverified.suggested_fix: Read `row["mu"]` directly and drop the comment. If pre-existing databases are genuinely a concern, add a real migration in `init_db()` (`ALTER TABLE images ADD COLUMN ...` guarded by a `PRAGMA table_info` check) rather than a read-only guard that leaves the write path broken.
